blocks.text: Summing constant local work over exactly `n` non-null calls gives `O(n)` time. The two child calls do not remain active as two full subtrees at once; depth-first execution completes one branch before the other, so the maximum number of live frames is the current path length, `O(h)`. On a balanced tree, `h = O(log n)`; on a skewed tree, `h = O(n)`. The result changes if the call contract revisits subtrees, copies path-sized state, or stores an explicit frontier, because those add work or memory not present in the stated contract.

feedback.reason: The call contract creates one constant-work call per node, while simultaneous recursive frames follow one root-to-leaf chain of length at most `h`.

blocks.text: In a proper rooted tree, child edges move strictly away from the root and no node is shared by two parents. A traversal therefore reaches each node once by construction. Graph DFS has a different subproblem contract because cycles or multiple incoming paths can revisit the same vertex, so visited state is part of correctness there. Tracking values is especially wrong because node identity, not value equality, determines whether two nodes are distinct. If the input were only “node references that may form a graph,” the contract would change and a visited set would become necessary.
